# Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling

Also called: Dynamic NeRF, 4D Radiance Fields, Temporal NeRF

## Overview
Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling extends static neural radiance fields to represent and render scenes that change over time, solving the limitation of standard NeRF which assumes a static environment . It differs from sibling methods by varying the approach to temporal encoding: some treat time as a direct coordinate input, others use canonical space warping with deformation fields, and others decompose the scene into static and dynamic components or stratify it by motion scale .

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of mapping a 4D space-time coordinate $(\mathbf{x}, t)$ to radiance properties (density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$). The rendering equation is adapted to integrate along rays at a specific time $t$:

$$
C(\mathbf{r}, t) = \int_{s_n}^{s_f} T(s, t) \sigma(\mathbf{r}(s), t) \mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r}(s), \mathbf{d}, t) ds
$$

where $\mathbf{r}(s) = \mathbf{o} + s\mathbf{d}$ is the ray equation and $T(s, t)$ is the accumulated transmittance at time $t$ [Parent](15546-dynamic-scene-and-temporal-modeling.md).

## Subtopics

### [Gear-NeRF](13848-gear-nerf.md)
Uses semantic segmentation to stratify the scene into "gears" based on motion scale, assigning higher-resolution 4D feature volumes to regions with larger motion.

### [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md)
Treats time $t$ as a direct input coordinate alongside space and view direction, serving as a baseline dynamic NeRF approach.

### [Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis](15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md)
Models a static canonical radiance field and differentially warps it to target time steps using average splatting and an inpaint network to handle occlusions.

### [Dynamic Appearance Particle Neural Radiance Field](15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md)
Decomposes the scene into a static grid-based field and a dynamic particle-based field, using monocular video data without multi-view stereo.

### [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md)
Models the 4D radiance field as a dynamic system estimated via a Kalman filter, separating motion estimation into an observer branch and a predictor branch using a tri-plane representation.

## Background
The concept of dynamic neural radiance fields emerged as an extension of the original NeRF paper [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md] to handle video sequences and dynamic scenes. Early approaches like [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md) introduced time as a direct input, while later methods such as [Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis](15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md) and [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md) introduced more complex deformation and filtering mechanisms to handle complex dynamics and occlusions .
